body.name: explain
body.doc: If true, returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.

body.name: ext
body.doc: Configuration of search extensions defined by Elasticsearch plugins.

body.name: from
body.doc:
Starting document offset. By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000
hits using the from and size parameters. To page through more hits, use the
search_after parameter.

body.name: track_total_hits
body.doc:
Number of hits matching the query to count accurately. If true, the exact
number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance. If false, the
response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.
Defaults to 10,000...

body.name: indices_boost
body.doc: Boosts the _score of documents from specified indices.

body.name: docvalue_fields
body.doc:
Array of wildcard (*) patterns. The request returns doc values for field
names matching these patterns in the hits.fields property of the response.

body.name: knn
body.doc: Defines the approximate kNN search to run.

body.name: min_score
body.doc:
Minimum _score for matching documents. Documents with a lower _score are
not included in search results and results collected by aggregations.

body.name: query
body.doc: Defines the search definition using the Query DSL.

body.name: script_fields
body.doc: Retrieve a script evaluation (based on different fields) for each hit.

body.name: size
body.doc:
The number of hits to return. By default, you cannot page through more
than 10,000 hits using the from and size parameters. To page through more
hits, use the search_after parameter.

body.name: _source
body.doc:
Indicates which source fields are returned for matching documents. These
fields are returned in the hits._source property of the search response.

body.name: fields
body.doc:
Array of wildcard (*) patterns. The request returns values for field names
matching these patterns in the hits.fields property of the response.

body.name: terminate_after
body.doc:
Maximum number of documents to collect for each shard. If a query reaches this
limit, Elasticsearch terminates the query early. Elasticsearch collects documents
before sorting. Defaults to 0, which does not terminate query execution early.

body.name: timeout
body.doc:
Specifies the period of time to wait for a response from each shard. If no response
is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
Defaults to no timeout.

body.name: track_scores
body.doc: If true, calculate and return document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.

body.name: version
body.doc: If true, returns document version as part of a hit.

body.name: seq_no_primary_term
body.doc:
If true, returns sequence number and primary term of the last modification
of each hit. See Optimistic concurrency control.

body.name: stored_fields
body.doc:
List of stored fields to return as part of a hit. If no fields are specified,
no stored fields are included in the response. If this field is specified, the _source
parameter defaults to false. You can pass _source: true to return both...

body.name: pit
body.doc:
Limits the search to a point in time (PIT). If you provide a PIT, you
cannot specify an <index> in the request path.

body.name: runtime_mappings
body.doc:
Defines one or more runtime fields in the search request. These fields take
precedence over mapped fields with the same name.

body.name: stats
body.doc:
Stats groups to associate with the search. Each group maintains a statistics
aggregation for its associated searches. You can retrieve these stats using
the indices stats API.

query.name: wait_for_completion_timeout
query.doc:
Blocks and waits until the search is completed up to a certain timeout.
When the async search completes within the timeout, the response won’t include the ID as the results are not stored in the cluster.

query.name: keep_alive
query.doc:
Specifies how long the async search needs to be available.
Ongoing async searches and any saved search results are deleted after this period.

query.name: keep_on_completion
query.doc: If `true`, results are stored for later retrieval when the search completes within the `wait_for_completion_timeout`.

query.name: allow_no_indices
query.doc:
Whether to ignore if a wildcard indices expression resolves into no concrete indices.
(This includes `_all` string or when no indices have been specified)

query.name: allow_partial_search_results
query.doc: Indicate if an error should be returned if there is a partial search failure or timeout

query.name: analyzer
query.doc: The analyzer to use for the query string

query.name: analyze_wildcard
query.doc: Specify whether wildcard and prefix queries should be analyzed

query.name: batched_reduce_size
query.doc:
Affects how often partial results become available, which happens whenever shard results are reduced.
A partial reduction is performed every time the coordinating node has received a certain number of new shard responses (5 by default).

query.name: ccs_minimize_roundtrips
query.doc: The default value is the only supported value.

query.name: default_operator
query.doc: The default operator for query string query (AND or OR)

query.name: df
query.doc: The field to use as default where no field prefix is given in the query string

query.name: docvalue_fields
query.doc: A comma-separated list of fields to return as the docvalue representation of a field for each hit

query.name: expand_wildcards
query.doc: Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both

query.name: explain

query.name: ignore_unavailable

query.name: lenient

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Wraps a filter query and returns every matching document with a relevance score equal to the `boost` parameter value.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: distance_feature
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Boosts the relevance score of documents closer to a provided origin date or point.
For example, you can use this query to give more weight to documents closer to a certain date or location.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: exists
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain an indexed value for a field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: function_score
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: The `function_score` enables you to modify the score of documents that are retrieved by a query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: fuzzy
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain terms similar to the search term, as measured by a Levenshtein edit distance.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: geo_bounding_box
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches geo_point and geo_shape values that intersect a bounding box.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: geo_distance
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches `geo_point` and `geo_shape` values within a given distance of a geopoint.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: match_none
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches no documents.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: match_phrase

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: match_phrase_prefix

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: more_like_this

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: multi_match
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Enables you to search for a provided text, number, date or boolean value across multiple fields.
The provided text is analyzed before matching.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: nested
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Wraps another query to search nested fields.
If an object matches the search, the nested query returns the root parent document.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: parent_id
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns child documents joined to a specific parent document.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: percolate
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches queries stored in an index.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: pinned
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Promotes selected documents to rank higher than those matching a given query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: prefix
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain a specific prefix in a provided field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: query_string
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents based on a provided query string, using a parser with a strict syntax.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: range
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain terms within a provided range.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: rank_feature
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Boosts the relevance score of documents based on the numeric value of a `rank_feature` or `rank_features` field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: regexp
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain terms matching a regular expression.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: script
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Filters documents based on a provided script.
The script query is typically used in a filter context.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: script_score
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Uses a script to provide a custom score for returned documents.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: semantic
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: A semantic query to semantic_text field types

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: shape
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Queries documents that contain fields indexed using the `shape` type.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: simple_query_string
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents based on a provided query string, using a parser with a limited but fault-tolerant syntax.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_containing
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns matches which enclose another span query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_field_masking
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Wrapper to allow span queries to participate in composite single-field span queries by _lying_ about their search field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_first
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches spans near the beginning of a field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_multi
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Allows you to wrap a multi term query (one of `wildcard`, `fuzzy`, `prefix`, `range`, or `regexp` query) as a `span` query, so it can be nested.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_near
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Matches spans which are near one another.
You can specify `slop`, the maximum number of intervening unmatched positions, as well as whether matches are required to be in-order.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_not
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Removes matches which overlap with another span query or which are within x tokens before (controlled by the parameter `pre`) or y tokens after (controlled by the parameter `post`) another span query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_or
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches the union of its span clauses.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_term
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Matches spans containing a term.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: span_within
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns matches which are enclosed inside another span query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: sparse_vector
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Using input query vectors or a natural language processing model to convert a query into a list of token-weight pairs, queries against a sparse vector field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: term
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Returns documents that contain an exact term in a provided field.
To return a document, the query term must exactly match the queried field's value, including whitespace and capitalization.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: terms
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Returns documents that contain one or more exact terms in a provided field.
To return a document, one or more terms must exactly match a field value, including whitespace and capitalization.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: terms_set
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc:
Returns documents that contain a minimum number of exact terms in a provided field.
To return a document, a required number of terms must exactly match the field values, including whitespace and capitalization.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: text_expansion
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Uses a natural language processing model to convert the query text into a list of token-weight pairs which are then used in a query against a sparse vector or rank features field.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: weighted_tokens
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Supports returning text_expansion query results by sending in precomputed tokens with the query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: wildcard
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: Returns documents that contain terms matching a wildcard pattern.

_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.name: wrapper
_types.query_dsl.QueryContainer.doc: A query that accepts any other query as base64 encoded string.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: allow_leading_wildcard
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, the wildcard characters `*` and `?` are allowed as the first character of the query string.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: analyzer
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Analyzer used to convert text in the query string into tokens.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: analyze_wildcard
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: auto_generate_synonyms_phrase_query
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, match phrase queries are automatically created for multi-term synonyms.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: default_field
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc:
Default field to search if no field is provided in the query string.
Supports wildcards (`*`).
Defaults to the `index.query.default_field` index setting, which has a default value of `*`.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: default_operator
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Default boolean logic used to interpret text in the query string if no operators are specified.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: enable_position_increments
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, enable position increments in queries constructed from a `query_string` search.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fields
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Array of fields to search. Supports wildcards (`*`).

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fuzziness
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Maximum edit distance allowed for fuzzy matching.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fuzzy_max_expansions
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Maximum number of terms to which the query expands for fuzzy matching.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fuzzy_prefix_length
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Number of beginning characters left unchanged for fuzzy matching.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fuzzy_rewrite
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Method used to rewrite the query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: fuzzy_transpositions
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, edits for fuzzy matching include transpositions of two adjacent characters (for example, `ab` to `ba`).

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: lenient
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: If `true`, format-based errors, such as providing a text value for a numeric field, are ignored.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: max_determinized_states
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Maximum number of automaton states required for the query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: minimum_should_match
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Minimum number of clauses that must match for a document to be returned.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: phrase_slop
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Maximum number of positions allowed between matching tokens for phrases.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: query
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Query string you wish to parse and use for search.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: quote_analyzer
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc:
Analyzer used to convert quoted text in the query string into tokens.
For quoted text, this parameter overrides the analyzer specified in the `analyzer` parameter.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: quote_field_suffix
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc:
Suffix appended to quoted text in the query string.
You can use this suffix to use a different analysis method for exact matches.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: rewrite
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Method used to rewrite the query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: tie_breaker
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: How to combine the queries generated from the individual search terms in the resulting `dis_max` query.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: time_zone
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) offset or IANA time zone used to convert date values in the query string to UTC.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: type
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc: Determines how the query matches and scores documents.

_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.name: boost
_types.query_dsl.QueryStringQuery.doc:
Floating point number used to decrease or increase the relevance scores of the query.
Boost values are relative to the default value of 1.0.
A boost value between 0 and 1.0 decreases the relevance score.
A value greater than 1.0 increases...

_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureFunctionSigm.name: pivot
_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureFunctionSigm.doc: Configurable pivot value so that the result will be less than 0.5.

_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.name: field
_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.doc: `rank_feature` or `rank_features` field used to boost relevance scores.

_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.name: saturation
_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.doc: Saturation function used to boost relevance scores based on the value of the rank feature `field`.

_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.name: log

_types.query_dsl.RankFeatureQuery.name: linear

_types.query_dsl.RegexpQuery.name: flags
_types.query_dsl.RegexpQuery.doc: Enables optional operators for the regular expression.

_types.query_dsl.RegexpQuery.name: max_determinized_states

_types.query_dsl.ScriptScoreFunction.doc: A script that computes a score.

_types.query_dsl.ScriptScoreQuery.doc: Documents with a score lower than this floating point number are excluded from the search results.

_types.query_dsl.ShapeFieldQuery.doc: Queries using an inline shape definition in GeoJSON or Well Known Text (WKT) format.

Creates an array containing the...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: attachment
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: The attachment processor lets Elasticsearch extract file attachments in common formats (such as PPT, XLS, and PDF) by using the Apache text extraction library Tika.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: bytes
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts a human readable byte value (for example `1kb`) to its value in bytes (for example `1024`).
If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.
Supported human readable units are "b", "kb", "mb", "gb",...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: circle
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Converts circle definitions of shapes to regular polygons which approximate them.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: community_id
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Computes the Community ID for network flow data as defined in the
Community ID Specification. You can use a community ID to correlate network
events related to a single flow.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: convert
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts a field in the currently ingested document to a different type, such as converting a string to an integer.
If the field value is an array, all members will be converted.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: csv
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Extracts fields from CSV line out of a single text field within a document.
Any empty field in CSV will be skipped.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: date
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Parses dates from fields, and then uses the date or timestamp as the timestamp for the document.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: date_index_name
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: The purpose of this processor is to point documents to the right time based index based on a date or timestamp field in a document by using the date math index name support.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: dissect
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Extracts structured fields out of a single text field by matching the text field against a delimiter-based pattern.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: dot_expander
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Expands a field with dots into an object field.
This processor allows fields with dots in the name to be accessible by other processors in the pipeline.
Otherwise these fields can’t be accessed by any processor.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: drop
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Drops the document without raising any errors.
This is useful to prevent the document from getting indexed based on some condition.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: enrich
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: The `enrich` processor can enrich documents with data from another index.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: fail
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Raises an exception.
This is useful for when you expect a pipeline to fail and want to relay a specific message to the requester.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: fingerprint
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Computes a hash of the document’s content. You can use this hash for
content fingerprinting.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: foreach
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Runs an ingest processor on each element of an array or object.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: ip_location
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Currently an undocumented alias for GeoIP Processor.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: geo_grid
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts geo-grid definitions of grid tiles or cells to regular bounding boxes or polygons which describe their shape.
This is useful if there is a need to interact with the tile shapes as spatially indexable fields.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: geoip
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: The `geoip` processor adds information about the geographical location of an IPv4 or IPv6 address.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: grok
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Extracts structured fields out of a single text field within a document.
You choose which field to extract matched fields from, as well as the grok pattern you expect will match.
A grok pattern is like a regular expression that supports...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: gsub
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts a string field by applying a regular expression and a replacement.
If the field is an array of string, all members of the array will be converted.
If any non-string values are encountered, the processor will throw an exception.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: html_strip
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Removes HTML tags from the field.
If the field is an array of strings, HTML tags will be removed from all members of the array.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: inference
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Uses a pre-trained data frame analytics model or a model deployed for natural language processing tasks to infer against the data that is being ingested in the pipeline.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: join
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Joins each element of an array into a single string using a separator character between each element.
Throws an error when the field is not an array.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: json
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Parses a string containing JSON data into a structured object, string, or other value.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: kv
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: This processor helps automatically parse messages (or specific event fields) which are of the `foo=bar` variety.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: lowercase
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts a string to its lowercase equivalent.
If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: network_direction
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Calculates the network direction given a source IP address, destination IP
address, and a list of internal networks.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: pipeline
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Executes another pipeline.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: redact
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
The Redact processor uses the Grok rules engine to obscure text in the input document matching the given Grok patterns.
The processor can be used to obscure Personal Identifying Information (PII) by configuring it to detect known patterns...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: registered_domain
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Extracts the registered domain (also known as the effective top-level
domain or eTLD), sub-domain, and top-level domain from a fully qualified
domain name (FQDN). Uses the registered domains defined in the Mozilla
Public Suffix List.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: remove
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: rename
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:

If the field doesn’t exist or the new name is already used, an exception will be thrown.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: reroute

When the `destination` option is not set, this...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:

The script runs in the `ingest` context.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc: Sets user-related details (such as `username`, `roles`, `email`, `full_name`, `metadata`, `api_key`, `realm` and `authentication_type`) from the current authenticated user to the current document by pre-processing the ingest.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: sort
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Sorts the elements of an array ascending or descending.
Homogeneous arrays of numbers will be sorted numerically, while arrays of strings or heterogeneous arrays of strings + numbers will be sorted lexicographically.
Throws an error when...

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: split
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Splits a field into an array using a separator character.
Only works on string fields.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: terminate
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Terminates the current ingest pipeline, causing no further processors to be run.
This will normally be executed conditionally, using the `if` option.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: trim
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Trims whitespace from a field.
If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be trimmed.
This only works on leading and trailing whitespace.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: uppercase
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Converts a string to its uppercase equivalent.
If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be converted.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: urldecode
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
URL-decodes a string.
If the field is an array of strings, all members of the array will be decoded.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: uri_parts
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
Parses a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) string and extracts its components as an object.
This URI object includes properties for the URI’s domain, path, fragment, port, query, scheme, user info, username, and password.

ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.name: user_agent
ingest._types.ProcessorContainer.doc:
The `user_agent` processor extracts details from the user agent string a browser sends with its web requests.
This processor adds this information by default under the `user_agent` field.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: actual_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: The field of the index which contains the ground truth. The data type of this field can be boolean or integer. If the data type is integer, the value has to be either 0 (false) or 1 (true).

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: predicted_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: The field in the index which contains the predicted value, in other words the results of the classification analysis.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: top_classes_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: The field of the index which is an array of documents of the form { "class_name": XXX, "class_probability": YYY }. This field must be defined as nested in the mappings.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: metrics
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: Specifies the metrics that are used for the evaluation.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: auc_roc
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: The AUC ROC (area under the curve of the receiver operating characteristic) score and optionally the curve. It is calculated for a specific class (provided as "class_name") treated as positive.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: class_name
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: Name of the only class that is treated as positive during AUC ROC calculation. Other classes are treated as negative ("one-vs-all" strategy). All the evaluated documents must have class_name in the list of their top classes.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.name: include_curve
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationClassificat.doc: Whether or not the curve should be returned in addition to the score. Default value is false.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.name: classification
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.doc: Classification evaluation evaluates the results of a classification analysis which outputs a prediction that identifies to which of the classes each document belongs.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.name: outlier_detection
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.doc: Outlier detection evaluates the results of an outlier detection analysis which outputs the probability that each document is an outlier.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.name: regression
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationContainer.doc: Regression evaluation evaluates the results of a regression analysis which outputs a prediction of values.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.name: actual_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.doc: The field of the index which contains the ground truth. The data type of this field can be boolean or integer. If the data type is integer, the value has to be either 0 (false) or 1 (true).

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.name: predicted_probability_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.doc: The field of the index that defines the probability of whether the item belongs to the class in question or not. It’s the field that contains the results of the analysis.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.name: metrics

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationOutlierDete.name: auc_roc

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.name: actual_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.doc: The field of the index which contains the ground truth. The data type of this field must be numerical.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.name: predicted_field
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.doc: The field in the index that contains the predicted value, in other words the results of the regression analysis.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.name: metrics
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegression.doc: Specifies the metrics that are used for the evaluation. For more information on mse, msle, and huber, consult the Jupyter notebook on regression loss functions.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.name: mse
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.doc: Average squared difference between the predicted values and the actual (ground truth) value. For more information, read this wiki article.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.name: msle
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.doc: Average squared difference between the logarithm of the predicted values and the logarithm of the actual (ground truth) value.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.name: r_squared
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.doc: Proportion of the variance in the dependent variable that is predictable from the independent variables.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.name: delta
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.doc: Approximates 1/2 (prediction - actual)2 for values much less than delta and approximates a straight line with slope delta for values much larger than delta. Defaults to 1. Delta needs to be greater than 0.

ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.name: offset
ml._types.DataframeEvaluationRegressionM.doc: Defines the transition point at which you switch from minimizing quadratic error to minimizing quadratic log error. Defaults to 1.

ml._types.DelayedDataCheckConfig.name: check_window

ml._types.DetectionRule.doc: The set of actions to be triggered when the rule applies. If more than one action is specified the effects of all actions are combined.

ml._types.DetectionRule.name: scope
ml._types.DetectionRule.doc: A scope of series where the rule applies. A rule must either have a non-empty scope or at least one condition. By default, the scope includes all series. Scoping is allowed for any of the fields that are also specified in `by_field_name`,...

ml._types.Detector.name: by_field_name
ml._types.Detector.doc: The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to their own history. It is used for finding unusual values in the context of the split.

ml._types.Detector.name: custom_rules
ml._types.Detector.doc: Custom rules enable you to customize the way detectors operate. For example, a rule may dictate conditions under which results should be skipped. Kibana refers to custom rules as job rules.

ml._types.Detector.name: detector_index
ml._types.Detector.doc: A unique identifier for the detector. This identifier is based on the order of the detectors in the `analysis_config`, starting at zero. If you specify a value for this property, it is ignored.

ml._types.Detector.name: exclude_frequent

ml._types.Detector.name: field_name
ml._types.Detector.doc: The field that the detector uses in the function. If you use an event rate function such as count or rare, do not specify this field. The `field_name` cannot contain double quotes or backslashes.

ml._types.Detector.name: function
ml._types.Detector.doc: The analysis function that is used. For example, `count`, `rare`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, or `sum`.

ml._types.Detector.name: over_field_name
ml._types.Detector.doc: The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to the history of all splits. It is used for finding unusual values in the population of all splits.

ml._types.Detector.name: partition_field_name
ml._types.Detector.doc: The field used to segment the analysis. When you use this property, you have completely independent baselines for each value of this field.

ml._types.Detector.name: use_null
ml._types.Detector.doc: Defines whether a new series is used as the null series when there is no value for the by or partition fields.

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: by_field_name
ml._types.DetectorRead.doc: The field used to split the data. In particular, this property is used for analyzing the splits with respect to their own history. It is used for finding unusual values in the context of the split.

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: custom_rules

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: detector_index

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: exclude_frequent
ml._types.DetectorRead.doc: If set, frequent entities are excluded from influencing the anomaly results. Entities can be considered frequent over time or frequent in a population. If you are working with both over and by fields, you can set `exclude_frequent` to...

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: field_name
ml._types.DetectorRead.doc: The field that the detector uses in the function. If you use an event rate function such as count or rare, do not specify this field. The `field_name` cannot contain double quotes or backslashes.

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: partition_field_name

ml._types.DetectorRead.name: use_null

ml._types.DetectorUpdate.name: custom_rules
ml._types.DetectorUpdate.doc:

has a predefined...

ml._types.Hyperparameter.doc: A positive number showing how much the parameter influences the variation of the loss function. For hyperparameters with values that are not specified by the user but tuned during hyperparameter optimization.

ml._types.Hyperparameter.name: relative_importance
ml._types.Hyperparameter.doc: A number between 0 and 1 showing the proportion of influence on the variation of the loss function among all tuned hyperparameters. For hyperparameters with values that are not specified by the user but tuned during hyperparameter...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: alpha
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly.
This parameter affects loss calculations by acting as a multiplier...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: lambda
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set.
Multiplies an L2 regularization term which applies to leaf weights of the individual trees in the forest.
A high lambda value causes...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: gamma
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Regularization parameter to prevent overfitting on the training data set.
Multiplies a linear penalty associated with the size of individual trees in the forest.
A high gamma value causes training to prefer...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: eta
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
The shrinkage applied to the weights.
Smaller values result in larger forests which have a better generalization error.
However, larger forests cause slower training.
By default, this value is calculated...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: eta_growth_rate_per_tree
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Specifies the rate at which `eta` increases for each new tree that is added to the forest.
For example, a rate of 1.05 increases `eta` by 5% for each extra tree.
By default, this value is calculated during...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: feature_bag_fraction
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Defines the fraction of features that will be used when selecting a random bag for each candidate split.
By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: downsample_factor
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Controls the fraction of data that is used to compute the derivatives of the loss function for tree training.
A small value results in the use of a small fraction of the data.
If this value is set to be less...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: max_attempts_to_add_tree
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
If the algorithm fails to determine a non-trivial tree (more than a single leaf), this parameter determines how many of such consecutive failures are tolerated.
Once the number of attempts exceeds the threshold, the forest training stops.

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: max_optimization_rounds_per_hyperparameter
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
A multiplier responsible for determining the maximum number of hyperparameter optimization steps in the Bayesian optimization procedure.
The maximum number of steps is determined based on the number of...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Defines the maximum number of decision trees in the forest.
The maximum value is 2000.
By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: num_folds
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc: The maximum number of folds for the cross-validation procedure.

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: num_splits_per_feature
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc: Determines the maximum number of splits for every feature that can occur in a decision tree when the tree is trained.

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: soft_tree_depth_limit
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.
Machine learning uses loss guided tree growing, which means that the decision trees grow where the regularized loss decreases most quickly.
This soft limit combines with the `soft_tree_depth_tolerance` to...

ml._types.Hyperparameters.name: soft_tree_depth_tolerance
ml._types.Hyperparameters.doc:
Advanced configuration option.

By default, this value is calculated during hyperparameter optimization.
It must be greater...

ml._types.InferenceConfigUpdateContainer.doc: Named entity recognition configuration for inference.

data is...
